members.title: SP Azad arrested, several other police officers under surveillance
members.lead: Police Superintendent (SP) Abul Kalam Azad has been arrested in a crimes against humanity case over the killing of Nuruzzaman Jony, former general secretary of the Khilgaon Thana unit of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD), in what police described at the time as a gunfight. Since 14 November, two SPs and two additional SPs, including Azad, have been arrested. The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) arrested Azad from the In-Service Training Centre in Gazipur on Wednesday. . Speaking to Prothom Alo on Thursday, DMP Additional Commissioner (DB) Md Shafiqul Islam said Azad had been arrested in connection with the Nuruzzaman Jony murder case. He was working at the training centre in Gazipur. Azad, a native of Jhalakathi, is a 25th batch Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) police cadre officer. The other three officers arrested are Chattogram Range Reserve Force SP Mohammad Jahangir Alam and Additional SPs Abul Hasan and Md Rakibul Hasan. Jahangir Alam was arrested on the night of 14 November in a sedition case filed with Panchlaish police station in Chattogram city. The allegations against him include maintaining contact with leaders of the Awami League, whose activities have been banned in the country, and supplying them with confidential information from within the police force. Additional SP Abul Hasan was arrested in connection with the murder of ruling BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party) activist Mokbul Hossain in Dhaka. A Dhaka court ordered him to be sent to jail on Tuesday. DMP said today that 33rd BCS police cadre Rakibul Hasan would be shown arrested in a murder case filed with Paltan police station in the capital. . On 19 January 2015, Nuruzzaman Jony went to Dhaka Central Jail to visit his younger brother. His family alleged that police picked him up along with one of his associates from outside the prison. members.title: Hasina is a thorn in Bangladesh-India relations, India is also realising this: Humaiun Kobir
members.lead: India is also realising that Sheikh Hasina is a thorn in relations between Bangladesh and India, claimed Foreign Affairs State Minister Humaiun Kobir. He said India was also beginning to understand Hasina's "madness" and was finding itself in an uncomfortable situation because of her. Humaiun Kobir made these remarks in response to questions from journalists at a briefing at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday afternoon. He was asked about Indian Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal's statement on Wednesday that Sheikh Hasina's plans to return to Bangladesh voluntarily and Dhaka's request for her extradition were two separate matters. . In reply, Humaiun Kobir said there was no difficulty in understanding India's position on treating a person's voluntary return to their country separately from the issue of an extradition treaty. The movement of ordinary passengers or civilians was one matter, while the extradition treaty applied to criminals. He said Sheikh Hasina fell under the criminal category and had to be handed over under the extradition treaty. Sheikh Hasina fled to India as she was ousted from power on 5 August 2024 amid the mass uprising. She has been staying in India since then. On 17 November 2025, International Crimes Tribunal-1 sentenced her to death in a case involving crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising. . Asked whether Bangladesh had formally requested India to extradite Sheikh Hasina and others and whether discussions were under way with New Delhi on the matter, State Minister Humaiun Kobir said Bangladesh had made the extradition request and was now waiting for a response. Asked about the possibility of Sheikh Hasina returning to Bangladesh in December and whether she would be arrested if she went to a Bangladeshi mission, Humaiun Kobir said Hasina would not return in December.
